answer: Tie each agent's voting weight to a long-lived liquidity anchor it must keep posted in a shared lagoon of pooled collateral. Weight climbs a slow spiral: it compounds only through sustained, peer-audited work across many epochs, and collapses to zero the moment the anchor is pulled. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand wallets, but each must fund its own anchor and crawl the spiral up from nothing, so a thousand clones cost a thousand stakes and still carry no earned history.
